entries: What are the Sangam literature works?

Sangam literature is the oldest Tamil literature (about 300 BCE – 300 CE), grouped into Ettuthogai (eight anthologies, such as Purananuru and Akananuru) and Pathupattu (ten idylls). The poems are about love (akam) and war and public life (puram).
What are the five great epics of Tamil literature?
The five great Tamil epics (Aimperumkappiyangal): Silappatikaram, Manimekalai, Civaka Cintamani, Valayapathi and Kundalakesi.

Silappatikaram (The Tale of the Anklet), by Ilango Adigal, tells of Kannagi, whose husband Kovalan is wrongly executed in Madurai for stealing the queen's anklet. Kannagi proves his innocence with her own anklet and burns Madurai in her grief — a story of justice and chastity.
Manimekalai was written by Seethalai Sathanar. It follows Manimekalai, the daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi, who becomes a Buddhist nun.
What is the structure of Thirukkural?

The Thirukkural has 1,330 kurals (couplets) in 133 chapters of 10 each, in three books: Aram (virtue, 38 chapters), Porul (wealth and politics, 70 chapters) and Inbam (love, 25 chapters). Each kural has 7 words in two lines. Ask me "give me a thirukkural" or "kural on friendship".

Avvaiyar was a great Tamil poetess (the name was used by more than one poet). Her Aathichoodi and Kondrai Vendhan teach children good values in short lines, like "அறம் செய விரும்பு" (Love to do good).
Kambar (12th century) wrote Kamba Ramayanam, the Tamil version of the Ramayana, one of the finest works of Tamil poetry.
Bharathidasan (1891–1964), the 'Revolutionary Poet' (Puratchi Kavignar), was a disciple of Bharathiyar and wrote about Tamil pride, social reform and rationalism.
The Tamil months: Chithirai, Vaikasi, Aani, Aadi, Avani, Purattasi, Aippasi, Karthigai, Margazhi, Thai, Maasi and Panguni. The Tamil New Year (Puthandu) is on 1 Chithirai, around 14 April.
How many letters are in the Tamil alphabet?
Tamil has 247 letters: 12 vowels (uyir), 18 consonants (mei), 216 combined letters (uyirmei) and 1 special letter, aytham (ஃ).
What are the famous festivals of Tamil Nadu?

Famous Tamil Nadu festivals: Pongal (harvest, January), Tamil New Year (April), Karthigai Deepam (lamps, November–December), Deepavali, Aadi Perukku (river festival), Chithirai Thiruvizha in Madurai, and the Chennai Margazhi music season.
What are the famous foods of Tamil Nadu?
Famous Tamil foods: idli, dosa, pongal, sambar, rasam, vada, Chettinad chicken, biryani (Dindigul, Ambur), kothu parotta, payasam, filter coffee and Tirunelveli halwa.
Who were the three great Tamil dynasties?
The three crowned Tamil kingdoms (Moovendhar): the Cholas (Thanjavur, symbol: tiger), the Cheras (west coast, bow) and the Pandyas (Madurai, fish).
What did Raja Raja Chola achieve?

Raja Raja Chola I (reigned 985–1014 CE) made the Chola empire a great power, conquered Sri Lanka and the Maldives, and built the Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur. His son Rajendra Chola I sent a navy to Southeast Asia.

Keezhadi, near Madurai, is an archaeological site where excavations since 2015 found an urban settlement from about the 6th century BCE, with Tamil-Brahmi writing, showing early literacy and city life in the Sangam age.
What is the classical music of Tamil Nadu?

Carnatic music is the classical music of South India, centred in Tamil Nadu. The Trinity of Carnatic music: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri. The Chennai December music season is world famous.
What are the famous tourist places in Tamil Nadu?

Famous places in Tamil Nadu: Madurai Meenakshi Temple, Thanjavur Big Temple, Mahabalipuram shore temple, Rameswaram and the Pamban bridge, Kanyakumari (Vivekananda Rock, Thiruvalluvar statue), Ooty, Kodaikanal, Yercaud, Chennai Marina Beach, and Hogenakkal Falls.
